z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:a4cd6ab82c991e: {"text": "Squaring comes before subtracting, like dance steps done in order. Work out each square on its own: 6^2 = 36 and 4^2 = 16. Then subtract: 36 − 16 = 20."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:b127025473db89: {"text": "Exercise takes 50% and reading takes 20%, so the gap between them is 30 percentage points. A percentage point is just the space between two percent numbers. Like a steady dance count, subtract the smaller percent from the larger one, step by step."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:4ba169058506ca: {"text": "Here is the idea: each prism's volume comes from multiplying its three dimensions, and the two results are then added. Adding edge lengths instead, though tempting, fails because volume counts unit cubes, much as a crocheter multiplies stitches by rows."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:8afaa5f32237f6: {"text": "Counting each clap in order gives 1, 2, 3, 4, so Zoe makes 4 claps. It helps to let every clap land before moving to the next, the way an animator draws each frame in sequence. Next time, count slowly through each action in turn, and the total will come together naturally."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:637110a2288143: {"text": "Re- means again, and build means to make or put together, so rebuild means to make or put together again. Unlock looks tempting because it also starts with a prefix, but un- means to undo, not to do again. Check the prefix meaning first, and rebuild is the only fit."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:b01ff8ce4b3f2f: {"text": "It can feel natural to reach for six, yet that word would fit only if a rocket were added. Like undoing a single crochet stitch, the backward count steps down from five to four."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:2c3f062c9765eb: {"text": "The tempting pick is 'The mailbox whispered a secret,' but whispering gives the mailbox a human quality, which is personification. Hyperbole is deliberate overstatement, so the correct answer is 'I have eaten a million sandwiches,' which exaggerates the number eaten."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:11d9038a1056be: {"text": "An array is simply rows times columns, so 4 rows of 7 squares gives 4 × 7 = 28 unit squares. Picture it like laying out manga panels in a tidy grid, one row at a time. Next time, just multiply the number of rows by the squares in each row, and the total comes right out."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:f4c4a4df3f6113: {"text": "Counting backward means each number word drops by one. Taking one rocket away from five leaves four, so the next word is four. Like a back step in dancing, go down one number each time a rocket leaves."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:758d427881dbdb: {"text": "It's super common to count only the numbers you hear, 1, 2, 1, which lands on 3. Those numbers tell how many claps come in each group, not the total so far. Keep one running count and add each clap: 1, then 2 more makes 3, then 1 more makes 4."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:6831f99bcaa077: {"text": "Unlock is sneaky, but un- means undo. Re- means again; rebuild means to build again. Think of fixing a bike a second time."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:81730c4dfab203: {"text": "A tempting pick is unbroken, since it also starts with un-, but it just means not broken yet. Unbreakable means not able to be broken, because un- means not and -able means able to be. Spotting that -able ending is a handy trick for next time."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:baf8bbfef391b6: {"text": "Multiplying 5 × 3 × 2 gives 30, and 4 × 3 × 2 gives 24 cubic centimeters. It can be tempting to double one volume, yet the volumes differ, so adding 30 + 24 gives 54 cubic centimeters."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:0fdb8652cfdc2b: {"text": "A tempting move is adding 4 + 7 to get 11, but that only counts the two numbers once. Each of the 4 rows holds 7 squares, so think 4 groups of 7: 4 × 7 = 28. It's like a monster truck rally — count the whole row of cars, not just one spot."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:b2f487205e4144: {"text": "The proverb is not really about taking a long trip right away. It means a large achievement begins with one small action and needs steady progress. That's why Mia can keep taking small steps toward improving, like sharpening a knife bit by bit."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:7ebd69d7bcb337: {"text": "It's easy to count the three clapping moments and land on 3, but some moments hold more than one clap. Here's the friendly trick: count every single clap in order, 1, 2, 3, 4, so Zoe makes 4 claps."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:045ca083aaa457: {"text": "A percentage point is the plain gap between two percentages, found by subtracting one from the other. The tempting slip is reading the question as a percent change, which compares the parts by ratio instead of subtracting. Subtract 20 from 50 and the gap is 30 percentage points."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:44ea5637ea6329: {"text": "The tempting shortcut is to subtract first and square the difference: (6 − 4)^2 = 4. That fails because each exponent binds only to its own number, so the squares must be found before any subtraction. Evaluate 6^2 = 36 and 4^2 = 16, then subtract to get 20."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:fc94b07c75adfa: {"text": "Some say two, counting only the bottom fish. That misses the fish on top. Count each fish like each mushroom, so say three."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:54cff16379ed3a:
{"text": "Here is the idea behind this hiker's trip.
Total distance means every step counts, even backwards ones.
The tempting trick is cancelling left against right.
That slips because the hiker still walked those squares.
So add each leg: 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 squares.
Like keeping every fan fiction draft, even the scrapped ones."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:a1d8ae67722e6b: {"text": "Some think an empty bowl has no number. But zero is the number for none. Like finding no mushrooms, the count is still 0."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:36e28968fe7577: {"text": "The tempting idea is counting only the final spot. That fails because walking back still uses steps. Add every part: 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 squares."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:0be2b2d40a81a5: {"text": "To get the total volume, find each prism's volume, then add the two. Prism A: 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubic centimeters. Prism B: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24, and 30 + 24 = 54 cubic centimeters."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:671c27c620b08a:
{"text": "The question says there are no crackers in the bowl.
A tempting idea is that every count must be at least 1.
That idea seems fair, but a count can be zero when there is nothing to count.
Zero is the number that says how many there are when there are none.
It is like counting parts in an empty tractor toolbox; the count is zero.
So the answer is 0 crackers, because zero is the count for an empty bowl."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:cc90c22c9f01ea:
{"text": "Here is the idea, one step at a time.
First, look for one tall line standing straight up.
The letter l has that tall line but no slants.
The letter n has curved humps, not straight slants.
The letter k adds two slanted lines near the middle.
So k is the tall line with its two sidekicks."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:e5ff723e69d33f:
{"text": "One tempting idea is to say two by counting only the bottom pair.
That leaves out the top fish, so it does not count every fish.
Count the fish one at a time to find the counting word for the whole group.
There is one fish at the top and two fish at the bottom.
One and two together make three, so the counting word for the whole group is three.
It is like counting tractor parts: each part gets counted once."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:385073b20426f6:
{"text": "A large achievement starts with one small action.
It also needs steady progress, meaning regular little efforts.
A tempting idea is taking a long trip right away.
But the proverb is not about real travel at all.
Here is the idea: keep taking small steps toward improving.
Think of fan fiction written one page at a time."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:515d7dfedd8f08: {"text": "A k has one tall line and two diagonals. An l seems close, but it has no diagonals. Like mushroom hunting, check every stroke before naming it."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:ab602249fa8ddc: {"text": "The tempting choice is \"that,\" but \"that\" points to something farther away, not beside the speaker. The right word is \"this,\" because \"this\" points to one nearby thing."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:10b3e0989fb3db:
{"text": "The question says there are no crackers in the bowl.
A tempting idea is that a bowl must always hold at least 1 cracker.
That idea does not work, because no crackers means the bowl is empty.
Zero is the number we use when there is none of something.
It is like counting parts in an empty tractor bin; the count is zero.
So the bowl contains 0 crackers."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:06b24457f1868a: {"text": "It's easy to mix up \"that,\" but \"that\" points to something far away. Since the book is beside you, \"this\" fits one nearby thing."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:dffc22c1bf6e78: {"text": "Here is the idea: sweet, big, and happy tell taste, size, or feelings, not color. The color word is yellow, which is what a ripe banana looks like."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:51d0c2b0ce1f22: {"text": "Words like sweet, big, and happy tell other things, not color. A ripe banana is yellow, so yellow names its color."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:8ecc9730eecd36: {"text": "It can feel natural to start with the vertical stroke from the center, but the top bar comes first in standard manuscript. So a capital T starts at the upper left, goes across, then lifts for a separate downward stroke from the center."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:8f55da2b1ad3a5: {"text": "Sweet might feel tempting since ripe bananas taste sweet, but it describes taste, not color. The color word here is yellow, which tells how the banana looks."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:4d4458f39fb0cd: {"text": "It can feel natural to start at the center and go down first, but the top bar actually comes first. A capital T begins at the upper left: top bar first, then a separate vertical stroke from the center downward."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:08f66bd5458d11: {"text": "Here is the idea: choices with details or no kicking do not tell the event. 'I kick the ball, and my friend runs toward it' names both actions in Sara's drawing."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:ee5d5554db3878:
{"text": "The ending sound of a word is the last sound you hear when you say it.
In "lunch," the letters c and h work together at the end to make one /ch/ sound.
A pick that can fool you is "chin," because it also has the letters c and h.
In "chin," those letters sit at the start, so the word ends with the /n/ sound.
"Wish" and "fish" end with s and h, which make the /sh/ sound, not the /ch/ sound.
So the word that ends with the /ch/ sound is "lunch.""}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:4a9c63f23cc1ba: {"text": "A tempting pick like 'I am outside with you' shifts the focus to yourself, giving Nia nothing to answer. The best reply picks up on her words and asks her something, so she can answer and the chat keeps going."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:23eb87a950bd22: {"text": "Here's the idea: the tempting picks give details or skip the kicking, so they don't tell the event. The right words name both actions in Sara's drawing: I kick the ball, and my friend runs toward it."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:c08c7bb68bf63d: {"text": "A tempting pick like \"I am outside with you\" just repeats the scene instead of moving the talk forward. The best reply, \"What kind of bird is it?\", asks about Nia's idea and keeps the conversation going."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:1917bb7f942498: {"text": "The tempting picks describe details like the shirt or the grass, but they skip the kicking action. The best words name both events: kicking the ball and a friend running toward it."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:aa6db1216d1275: {"text": "The tempting move is starting with the down stroke, which makes sense, but standard manuscript draws the top bar first. So: start at the upper left, go across, lift, then the stroke from the center downward — hat before body."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:4f940bac3d7052: {"text": "It's tempting to draw the vertical line first, but the top bar goes first, like a beat before the drop. So: start at the upper left, go across, lift, then go down from the center."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:e609e45be1461f: {"text": "The tempting picks wander off to the sky or another bird, leaving Nia's news hanging. Asking what kind of bird it is responds to her idea and invites her to answer, so the conversation can go another turn."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:7334f4791f1e2a: {"text": "Saying you are outside too just talks about yourself instead of Nia's news. Asking what kind of bird it is keeps the chat going by inviting her to answer."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:3da831c21a7f63: {"text": "The tempting pick is 'to', but the child was already at school, so 'to' points the wrong way. 'From' names the starting point of the child's walk, which was school."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:7faf386363426d: {"text": "Segmenting, splitting a word into sounds, lists each sound in order, so 'pen' gives /p/, /e/, /n/. Starting with /e/ is tempting because that sound sits in the middle; segmenting follows the word's order."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:b6bb166336c0bc: {"text": "Here is the idea: 'from' identifies the starting point of the child's walk, which was school. The tempting choice 'to' fails here because it points toward a destination, and the child was already at school before walking away. So the fix is simply choosing 'from' — like noting where a longboard ride pushes off, it marks where the movement began."}
z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:c833ee4c30c6e4: {"text": "It's easy to think left and down keep the numbers positive, but both moves land in negative territory. Left makes x negative, down makes y negative, so the point is (-4, -3)."}
